---
title: "Bring your simulation bank"
---

METIS works on aggregate trajectories. Convert agent-level events or objects
into the scientific outcomes you want to emulate before loading them.

## Table format

| contact_rate | recovery_rate | rep | t | incidence | prevalence |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.4 | 0.1 | 0 | 1 | 12 | 40 |
| 0.4 | 0.1 | 0 | 2 | 15 | 48 |
| 0.4 | 0.1 | 1 | 1 | 10 | 38 |
| 0.4 | 0.1 | 1 | 2 | 14 | 45 |

One row is one timepoint from one replicate. Parameters repeat on every row.
`rep` is unique within a parameter group, not necessarily across the whole bank.

```python
from metis import SimulationDataset
bank = SimulationDataset.from_parquet(
    "bank.parquet", inputs=["contact_rate", "recovery_rate"],
    outputs=["incidence", "prevalence"],
)
```

`from_frame` accepts a Polars or pandas frame. `from_arrays` accepts input arrays
`(runs, inputs)` and output arrays `(runs, times, outputs)` with explicit column
names and optional time/group/replicate metadata.

## Validation and assumptions

Inputs and outputs must be finite and numeric. All runs need the same ordered
time grid, and static inputs must be constant within a run. Duplicate
observations, missing times, inconsistent horizons and nonnumeric values fail
with an explanation. No rows are silently dropped, no interpolation is done,
and no noise is added to constant values.

A shared irregular numeric time grid is accepted, but the models learn sequence
positions rather than an elapsed-time equation. Predictions use that fitted
grid; arbitrary new prediction times are not supported.

Constant dimensions use a standardization scale of one. Input/output statistics
are fitted on training data only and stored in the model. `constant_mask` makes
constant dimensions inspectable. A constant training input changing at inference
is extrapolation and triggers a range warning.

## Grouped or explicit splits

By default, identical input tuples define groups. Supply `groups=["scenario"]`
when, for example, initial conditions differ across replicates of a shared
parameter scenario. A scenario never straddles partitions.

```python
split = bank.split(validation_fraction=.2, test_fraction=.2, seed=42)
```

For already separated simulation banks:

```python
from metis import DatasetSplit
split = DatasetSplit.from_datasets(train_bank, validation_bank, test_bank)
```

Schemas, time grids and disjoint group identities are checked. Keep group keys
consistent across files; renaming the same scenario cannot establish scientific
independence. If there are too few groups to make requested nonempty partitions,
the split fails rather than producing empty training data.

The current loader materializes the bank in RAM. Training transfers minibatches
to the device, so the complete bank need not fit on the GPU. Very large banks
still require an out-of-core extension.

## Inspect without training

```bash
uv run metis inspect-data bank.parquet --inputs contact_rate recovery_rate --outputs incidence prevalence
```

This validates the requested schema and reports the available bank. It does not
fit a network or decide whether the simulation design answers your scientific
question. For CSV, use the [own-bank exercise](own-bank.qmd) to read a Polars
frame and save Parquet. Keep units and group meanings in your project metadata.

## Explicit preprocessing

The core loader does not truncate or reinterpret your data automatically. If
your scientific design requires starting later or using the first retained
output as an initial-condition input, opt in explicitly:

```python
from metis.preprocessing import truncate_simulations, initialize_static_inputs

bank = truncate_simulations(bank, start_time=10)
bank = initialize_static_inputs(bank, mapping={"initial_incidence": "incidence"})
split = bank.split(seed=42)
```

Truncation keeps observed times at or after the boundary without interpolating
or resetting the time coordinate. Initialization copies each realization's first
retained output into the named static input. Both preserve scenario/replicate
identities, so replicate-specific initial values do not split the original
scenario across partitions. Record the boundary and mapping as methodological
choices; they change the data and its fingerprint.

For known varying inputs, keep them as output-schema channels and select them
with `Surrogate(..., observed_outputs=[...])`. See [conditioning](conditioning.qmd)
for which channels are scored and what information each model may use.
